subject: Money
title: Too Big to Fail
description: A quick win: understand Too Big to Fail.

hook.text: The four largest US banks hold $10 trillion in assets. If one fails, the cascade could crash the global economy.

buildup.text: After 2008, regulators declared certain banks 'systemically important.' Too interconnected to let die.

discovery.text: These banks must hold more capital and pass stress tests. But they also get implicit government backing.

twist.text: The designation creates a competitive advantage. Lenders trust too-big-to-fail banks more, giving them cheaper funding.

climax.text: Protecting the biggest banks makes them bigger. The policy meant to prevent crisis plants seeds for the next one.

punchline.text: Too big to fail becomes too big to fix.

quiz.question: What advantage do 'too big to fail' banks have?
